What are the main findings?

Gene therapy for sickle cell disease has progressed from lentiviral gene addition strategies to precise genome editing approaches targeting fetal hemoglobin regulation or the β-globin mutation.

Clinical translation has demonstrated the feasibility of durable disease modification, but implementation remains constrained by conditioning toxicity, delivery challenges, and complex treatment pathways.
